item.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
item.description: A financially motivated threat activity cluster tracked as REF3364 has been attributed to a Linux-focused cryptocurrency mining operation that tampers with the readings used to detect high GPU workloads. Central to the intrusion is a toolkit called SANSAR , a Rust-based orchestrator that receives commands over the TOR anonymity network to manage CPU and GPU miners. The activity was observed in late October 2026. "The threat actor also deployed a kernel rootkit to hide selected processes and files, an NVIDIA Management Library ( NVML ) wrapper to falsify GPU readings, and a separate backdoor named netns," Elastic Security Labs said in a report published last week. "This backdoor retrieves its C2 [command-and-control] address from an Ethereum smart contract before connecting to the server directly." item.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
item.description: Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM , One API , and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records. The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys. The team said this week that it cannot verify the outcomes reported by the agents. It has moderate confidence that the agents ran on ARTEX , an open-source AI tool for penetration testing. The records include a playbook of known entry points for each targeted product. It lists default administrator credentials such as LiteLLM's default master key, unfinished installs that an outsider could take over, and known flaws in Langflow and RAGFlow . item.description: An investigation into suspicious activity within a Russian software developer's network has uncovered a months-long compromise of its development infrastructure and a software code-signing server. The activity, documented by Kaspersky's ICS CERT team after it was contacted by the affected developer in June 2025, has been attributed to a threat actor named BO Team (aka Black Owl, Hoody Hyena, and Lifting Zmiy). The name of the targeted company was not disclosed, but it operates from within Russia and develops software that has a "customer base in the Russian Federation," according to Kaspersky. Over the course of several months, the intrusion resulted in the theft of confidential information and the compromise of all components of the organization's IT infrastructure, including Windows and Linux servers, workstations, hypervisors, backup servers, security solution management servers, and network equipment. item.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
item.description: Meta was fined €805 million in Italy yesterday over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests photos and videos from users' phone galleries for them to post. The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, found that the feature was enabled by default and that the app accessed Italian users' photos, videos, and related metadata without their explicit consent. The company has 60 days to switch the feature off by default, including for people who have already granted the app gallery access, and to request consent separately. Meta plans to appeal and calls the fine "disproportionate", a spokesperson said in a statement reported by Reuters. The app asks for gallery access via a single permission that covers the whole app and several functions with different purposes, the authority found. item.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
item.description: The compromise of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace was the result of the theft of an access key that was exposed in the wake of a breach targeting Fireworks AI . "An attacker obtained an access key we had issued to Fireworks," Cursor said in a Friday update. "The key was exposed by Fireworks , and the attacker used it to copy data from a read-only storage bucket we used to share data with them." The disclosure comes nearly two weeks after a trojanized version of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension was distributed through Cursor Marketplace as a legitimate update, attempting to install a persistent SSH backdoor on affected systems.
